title: The Pandavas in Disguise at Virata's Court
text:
In the Mahabharata, the five Pandava brothers and their wife Draupadi lost a rigged game of dice. As part of their punishment they had to spend twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth year in hiding. If anyone discovered them during that final year, they would have to begin the whole exile again.

They decided to hide at the court of King Virata, and each chose a disguise that matched a real skill. Yudhishthira, the eldest, who loved dice, became the king's companion and gaming partner under the name Kanka. Bhima, the strongest and the greatest eater, became the royal cook and a wrestler. Arjuna, the great archer, disguised himself as Brihannala, a eunuch who taught music and dance to the princess. Nakula, who understood horses, took charge of the royal stables, and Sahadeva, who knew cattle, became a herdsman. Draupadi became a maid to the queen.

The year was full of danger. Bhima had to kill the queen's brother Kichaka secretly to protect Draupadi, and at the very end Arjuna fought off an invading army. But they kept their secret until the year was over, and then revealed themselves to an astonished king.
lesson: A team can survive a hard stretch when each person takes on the role that fits a real strength. Hiding well is easier when you play a part you already know how to do.
people: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadi, King Virata
